panels.title: Bytes served to clients vs fetched from origin
panels.description: No native 'cache bytes' counter exists. 'client response bytes' includes hits+misses; 'backend fetch bytes' fires only on a miss. Compare the two lines rather than reading either as pure cache traffic. NOTE: varnish_backend_response_bodybytes (the obvious-sounding name) is ALWAYS 0 for Docker Hub -- its blob storage redirects to a CDN, and Orca follows that via vmod_goto, so the real bytes land under backend_name="goto" in the byte_sum histogram, not under the named dockerhub_dir_1/2 backends. Use varnish_backend_response_bytes_byte_sum{byte_type="body"} instead.

panels.title: Origin request rate by registry
panels.description: Should drop sharply once the cache is warm. 'vcl' label is Orca's per-registry VCL group (dockerhub_g1, npmjs_g1, ...).

panels.title: Fetch latency — client-facing vs origin
panels.description: No pure hit-only histogram exists. Backend ttfb only fires on a miss (a real proxy for origin latency); client ttfb blends hits+misses (mostly hits once warm).

panels.title: Ruleset health
panels.description: Rules/rulesets currently loaded (gauges) and reload attempts by status. A drop to 0 on either gauge without a matching config change is worth investigating -- see the OSV startup-race finding in results/notes.md.
